subject: Archaeology
title: Karnak: The Largest Temple Ever Built
description: A fast breakdown of Karnak: The Largest Temple Ever Built for builders.

hook.text: Karnak Temple was so massive that Notre-Dame Cathedral could fit inside its main hall.

buildup.text: Thirty pharaohs expanded Karnak over 2,000 years. Each king added halls, obelisks, and statues.

discovery.text: The Hypostyle Hall contains 134 columns, each 70 feet tall, carved with hieroglyphs from floor to ceiling.

twist.text: In 1903, workers found a pit with 17,000 statues and fragments buried beneath the courtyard — a sacred dump.

climax.text: Karnak was not just a temple. It was a city — with workshops, granaries, and its own sacred lake.

punchline.text: Thirty kings built one temple for 2,000 years. Nobody ever said 'it's finished.'

quiz.question: What was found buried in a pit beneath Karnak's courtyard in 1903?
options: A hidden tomb of an unknown pharaoh
Over 17,000 statues and fragments in a sacred dump
Gold and silver offerings from visiting foreign kings
